title: Anterior Scalene Muscle Block for Diagnostic and Surgical Planning in Pediatric Thoracic Outlet Syndrome—Two Case Reports
content: Background: Thoracic Outlet Syndrome (TOS) is a rare and diagnostically challenging condition in pediatric populations, often presenting with vague symptoms such as paresthesia, weakness, and upper extremity discomfort. While the Anterior Scalene Muscle Block (ASMB) is a well-established diagnostic tool for neurogenic TOS (nTOS) in adults, its application in pediatric patients remains underreported. Case Presentations: We present two adolescent females with progressive upper extremity symptoms indicative of nTOS. Despite comprehensive evaluations, including imaging, specialist consultations, and conservative management, both patients did not experience symptom relief. Consequently, they were referred to the Acute Pain Service for further diagnostic evaluation, with a presumed diagnosis of nTOS. Ultrasound-guided ASMB was performed in both cases, resulting in immediate and significant symptom improvement, confirming neurovascular compression, and aiding surgical decision-making. Both patients underwent first rib resection with brachial plexus neurolysis. At one-month follow-up, both patients reported complete resolution of symptoms and a return to baseline function. Conclusions: These cases demonstrate the utility of ASMB as a diagnostic adjunct in pediatric patients with suspected nTOS, aiding in surgical decision-making. The block provides rapid confirmation of neurovascular compression, enabling timely surgical intervention and reducing diagnostic delays. This report highlights ASMB's potential role in managing pediatric TOS and emphasizes the need for further research to validate its effectiveness and refine diagnostic protocols for this population.
